column8: Mon 16 Nov: store, 3e custody set-up: SIPC's 30 or 60 day and six-month deadlines re-read today; drop or flag the customer-name clause (above $500,000), since Laura's holdings are in street name (Q72-020) and it does not reach her.
Mon 16 Nov: same SIPC claims process as row 1 (quotes re-read today); weeks is the floor overclaims: John Muir moved 8,000 accounts within 10 days and MJK about a week (Q72-014).

Mon 16 Nov: store, evidence for row 16: GAO 1992 re-read today (Muir 8,000 of 16,000 in 10 days, 4,700 more in 3 months; FDR 26,000 of 30,000 in 3 months); GAO adds that accounts of government bonds attract buyers fast.

Mon 16 Nov: store: Blinder Robinson about half at 6 months and a year in all, re-read today; Muir's last 7 months or more came from disputes over what customers owed Muir, which an account that borrows nothing cannot have.
Mon 16 Nov: store: GAO-11-707 and GAO-12-735 read only as search excerpts, so S 3; the LBI tail was institutions disputing customer status, not retail cash accounts.

Mon 16 Nov: search excerpt only (the CFTC 5133-05 page body did not load today); its fact is carried by row 12.
Mon 16 Nov: search excerpt of the MF Global prospectus only; Man Financial buying Refco LLC's accounts is carried by row 12; within weeks is Keel's reading.
Mon 16 Nov: store: RCM's commingled fungible pool; $4.16bn owed against $1.905bn (45.8%, Keel arithmetic checks) are complaint figures as quoted by the court.

Mon 16 Nov: store: 52.81% interim from 27 Dec 2006, 261 days after the 10 Apr 2006 appointment, re-read today in the trustee's fee application; fix the figure: the $1.486bn went to securities customers and general creditors, customers got $1,364.71m.
Mon 16 Nov: store: RCM's 99.7% for securities customers about a decade on (plan administrator's release filed as a court exhibit); evidence for row 12.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e backup to Q72-016 (kept apart is the variable, Rule 15c3-3, Q72-011): RCM's half verified (52.81% at 14 months, checks); Refco LLC's half rests on two search excerpts, so nothing lost is inference: read at source or say moved to a new broker within weeks.
Mon 16 Nov: Peregrine's first slice (30% and 40% within a few weeks via Vision Financial) is confirmed in the 2021 motion read today; row 14 carries the whole path.

Mon 16 Nov: store hygiene: grep shows store Q65-025 still says customers lost most of the money (the 2013 complaint's word, keep 18); out of date: the trustee's 8 Nov 2021 motion, re-read today, authorises 72.16% to domestic 4d and 100% to foreign 30.7 customers, over $290m to over 8,000 holders, so Q65-025 needs lost most at first plus these figures; this row is VERIFIED, the conflict is with the store row; futures and theft, no part for Laura.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: a negligent keeper paid $18m (CFTC 2015); futures segregation, no part for Laura.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e custody line, the measured wait behind Q72-017 (a broker failure costs time, weeks for a cash account of Treasuries): reconcile MF Global's 318 accounts with Q72-017's about 330 before use; LBI's 4.7 years and the decade-long tails were disputed or pooled property, never a segregated cash account.
Mon 16 Nov: store, background for rows 20-22: $62.5bn, $785m of Lehman paper (1.26%, checks) and the $0.97 low confirmed in Makhija 2025 (which dates the $62.5bn to 12 Sep).
Mon 16 Nov: store only: who bears a run's loss in a $1.00 fund (the $10.83bn paid on 15 Sep confirmed in Makhija); Laura never redeems and her funds pay at their ends.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e aha candidate at most: State Street quote verbatim in Makhija's timeline; reword never needs its custodian to lend as does not rely on its custodian's credit to pay holders (in-kind redemption checked in the SAIs); never set the 2008 act beside IBTP or VT as a warning.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e parallel for a frozen fund (late, pro rata): Makhija Figure 4 re-read today, 50.8% on 30 Oct 2008 and 78.9% on 3 Dec, of assets at the close on 15 Sep; 45 and 79 days check; the Primary held commercial paper, her funds hold Treasuries.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e or store: 98.6% on 29 Jan 2010 (501 days checks; SEC 2010-16: more than 98 cents), 99.0% on 16 Jul 2010 and 99.1% final on 9 Dec 2014, all re-read today.
Mon 16 Nov: store: why the wait was long (SEC 2010-16: approximately 30 lawsuits); Makhija dates the $3.5bn special reserve to the 3 Dec 2008 plan, announced 26 Feb 2009, so date it so.
Mon 16 Nov: VeriSign's 10-Q read only as a search excerpt; its 50% on 31 Oct 2008 is row 20's first slice seen by one holder.

Mon 16 Nov: store, extends Q2a-019: the government-paper fund was made whole only with Treasury as buyer; it held agency paper and was a $1.00 fund, unlike an iBond ETF; never a third reason to change.

Mon 16 Nov: store: money ran into Treasury funds in 2008 (ICI's own account; Makhija cites Bernanke's $362bn into government funds, 10 Sep-1 Oct); pair with row 24, which held $1.00 only with Treasury's help.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e, the honest limit for the fund rungs and the floor: a frozen fund pays late and pro rata, it does not lose Treasuries; in-kind settlement through the Federal Reserve System confirmed in the 2026 SAI; never say a Treasury fund cannot freeze (row 24).

Mon 16 Nov: store, 2.1 note: the 2026 iBonds SAI's lists re-read today (JPMorgan: Dec 2026-2033, Dec 2035, 2045, 2055 Treasury funds; State Street: Dec 2034, 2044, 2054), so IBTM, IBTO and IBTQ are with JPMorgan; closes Q72-025's UNVERIFIED.

Mon 16 Nov: store: IBTP (Dec 2034) is on the 2026 SAI's State Street list, re-read today; JPMorgan only for securities lending.
Mon 16 Nov: store: VT's custodian is State Street (Vanguard International Equity Index Funds SAI, re-read today); VT is the money not yet promised.

Mon 16 Nov: store, 3e clause at most: the 3 May 2024 supplement, re-read today, moved the Dec 2032 and Dec 2033 Treasury funds from State Street to JPMorgan on or around 6 May 2024 with nothing for holders to do; a keeper is a replaceable contractor (pairs with Q72-030).
Mon 16 Nov: store only: gross lending income $5,896 (Dec 2034) and $18,223 (Dec 2035), Dec 2033 N/A, re-read in the SAI; Q26-015 and Q72-027 carry lending.

Mon 16 Nov: store or 3e: 17 CFR 450.3 exempts banks that hold government securities under their regulator's fiduciary standards, so never say 450.4 binds JPMorgan and State Street; say segregation free of liens is required by 450.4 or equivalent fiduciary rules.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e custody line, the bank half beside Q72-008's broker half: custody assets remain the owner's if a bank fails (OCC); cite the OCC sentence, since 12 CFR 51 covers uninsured national banks and JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. is insured.

Mon 16 Nov: store, adds the legal basis to Q72-026: Rule 17f-5 governs foreign custodians only, so it backs VT's foreign shares, not IBTM's US custody; say a fund's brief cash at its custodian is the one bank-credit point, never that a custodian could cost Laura holdings; money funds at the end is inference from IBTA.
Mon 16 Nov: store, 3e limit: safe in law, not instant in practice; a lawyer's argument, no case; quote it for time only, never its could limit recovery about Laura's holdings.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: VT's foreign shares under Rule 17f-5's contract terms; VT is the money not yet promised.

Mon 16 Nov: store only: REX release read only as a search excerpt; an early closure of a small sponsor's fund, unlike IBTM's planned end; Q3c-010 has the ended iBond Treasury funds at 3-7 days.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e and Table 3's default row: CRS re-read today ($125,000 forgone on about $122m, 0.10% Keel arithmetic checks; no authority to reimburse; normal by 14 May); CRS's $125,000 cites a 2012 self-published book; a 1979-length delay would pass the five-business-day test but touched no book entry (pairs with Q15-015, Q15-030); never no compensation (row 42).

Mon 16 Nov: store hygiene, re-read in CRS: a settlement offer that reportedly more than 80% accepted, H.R. 6054 died, the suit dismissed with prejudice on 12 May 1980; corrects Q15-015's note (with no compensation) and confirms Q15-016's refusal (no new law).
